narrative_purpose: Reveal the large internal motion hidden beneath a nearly calm tide and show how breaking against reef relief can mix a stratified water column.
subject: A narrow alien reef pass in cutaway. The sea surface crosses the frame as a nearly level, gently rippled line. Far beneath it, three translucent density layers bend into one broad internal wave as tidal flow passes a steep submarine ridge. On the downstream face the wave steepens and breaks into a compact cloud of teal turbulence, lifting sparse nutrient-like particles toward the illuminated upper water. The surface above shows only a small disturbance.
scene: A scientifically legible Pandoran reef-channel cross-section connecting a sheltered turquoise lagoon to dark open ocean, focused on submerged water structure rather than animals.
camera: Wide side-on underwater cutaway, with the reef ridge in the lower centre, calm surface across the upper fifth, incoming layered water on the left and breaking turbulence on the right.
light: Soft cyan daylight confined to the upper water, indigo depth, pale magenta density interfaces and restrained living-teal turbulence at the slope.
palette: Void indigo, ocean teal, cyan surface light, muted magenta layer boundaries and a compact living-teal mixing plume.
style: Painterly naturalist ocean-process plate with cinematic depth and physically readable layers, not a flat educational diagram.
detail_level: Three clear bent density bands, one steep reef ridge, one compact breaking zone and broad uncluttered water for later callouts.
composition: The visual contrast must be between the quiet surface and the much larger submerged wave; reserve negative space at upper left, centre and lower right for annotations.
consistency_notes: Match the marine palette and painterly material of fig-03. Render motion using bent particle fields and density interfaces, never arrows. Keep the claim generic rather than depicting a confirmed Awa'atlu measurement.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no giant breaking surface wave, no tsunami, no weather map, no vector infographic, no glossy CGI
